title: 2 Years Later, One Piece Finally Solves One of Its Biggest Mysteries About the Sun God and Luffy
content:
The One Piece manga is currently deep into the action-packed climax of the Elbaph arc, delivering the necessary power upgrades to its main characters. However, amidst all the action, the series has not forgotten to resolve some of its underlying mysteries. It has always been a pattern for One Piece to introduce several mysteries early on and gradually solve them during major climactic events. The fight in the Elbaph arc has revolved around the Straw Hats mastering Supreme King Haki to take down their opponents, which is particularly important since the new villains can only be defeated through this power. While Zoro has always possessed this ability, with the latest arc further solidifying his mastery, Sanji was still left behind.

However, the past few chapters have seemingly resolved Sanji’s complications , with the latest chapter further solidifying that he has almost mastered this power. This also comes alongside a strong declaration from Sanji, stating that Zoro can be Luffy’s sword while he will be his shield. This gives the two characters more defined roles, particularly Sanji, as Zoro has always been associated with his swordsmanship, while Sanji now takes on the role of the protector. What makes this even more intriguing, however, is that this declaration aligns with the depiction of the Sun God revealed earlier in the arc, who wields a shield and a sword as his weapons of choice. It now seems that Eiichiro Oda deliberately established this parallel.

One Piece Chapter 1197 Finally Solves a Major Sun God Mystery

Elbaph revealed a striking detail about the Sun God when the subject was first discussed in Chapter 1136, where Elder Jarul explained that there are different interpretations of Sun God Nika . While some revere him, others fear him as the God of Destruction. The intriguing detail was that this chapter featured one of the clearest depictions of the Sun God, which bore a striking resemblance to Luffy’s Gear 5, notably wielding a shield and a sword. In the Harley mural revealed a couple of chapters later, the Sun God’s depiction for the Third World once again featured a spear and a shield. Considering that this Third World revolves around Luffy, as the Sun God leading the rebellion against Imu and the World Government, the sword and shield could represent Zoro and Sanji.

Luffy is a fighter who does not rely on weapons, instead using his Devil Fruit and Haki as his primary tools. This means the deliberate choice to depict the Sun God with a sword and shield could represent the two important assets of the current Sun God: Zoro and Sanji. On closer inspection, the small detail of the sword being in the Sun God’s right hand while the shield is in his left also represents their importance and what they mean to Luffy. Both are equally important to him, and without either of them, Luffy would struggle to fulfill his dream of becoming the Pirate King.

One Piece author Eiichiro Oda has a habit of foreshadowing important elements from the very beginning, and it is once again amazing to see how Zoro and Sanji’s endgame roles for Luffy may have been hidden in plain sight. While this is a major development for Sanji and further highlights what both characters mean to Luffy and the Sun God, there are surely many more upgrades to come for them. The Final Saga will likely bring even more significant power-ups for Zoro and Sanji as their roles alongside Luffy become increasingly intertwined with the prophecy of Sun God Nika.

title: Shonen Jump’s Most Underrated Magical Action-Comedy Series Is Set to Take Over 2027
content:
Shonen Jump ‘s most underrated magical action-comedy series, which debuted in 2020, is getting a special revival in 2027. Over the past few years, Shonen Jump magazine has undergone significant changes. The most notable has been the shift toward shorter manga runs, with the magazine now more willing than ever to cancel series. One series that perfectly represents this shorter model while offering a unique narrative is actually Mashle: Magic and Muscles by Hajime Komoto, which first debuted in January 2020. The manga emerged as an intriguing new leading shonen series.

Like most popular manga series, it received an anime adaptation three years later, bringing its fun premise to life through A-1 Pictures, along with a banger of an opening theme for the first season that remains a fan favorite. However, the manga came to an end in 2023, shortly after the first season concluded. Although the anime’s second season arrived the following year, in 2024, the series has remained silent for almost three years. Recently, however, several details have emerged about the franchise, highlighting how it is secretly preparing to dominate Winter and Spring 2027 with two projects that could also give the manga a boost.

Shonen Jump’s Most Underrated 2020 Action-Comedy Is Set to Dominate 2027 With Two Major Projects

The Mashle: Magic and Muscles anime is set to return with a new season, picking up the story where the second season left off in March 2024. The new season will continue adapting the Divine Visionary Exam arc, which had already begun to gain fans’ attention. This exciting arc will continue as fans get to see how Mash’s muscles overcome the challenges presented by the upcoming events. It will bring the series closer to the manga’s original conclusion, and by the time the season ends, a fourth and final season of the anime could also be announced. However, the biggest project set to boost the franchise next year is its surprising live-action adaptation.

A few days ago, it was announced that the Mashle live-action movie is in production and nearing completion , with the announcement also revealing its release date. The film will arrive in Japanese theaters on March 19, 2027. Warner Bros. and Fuji TV are distributing the project, while CREDEUS is handling production. The studio has been working on live-action movie adaptations for some time, including the recent Sakamoto Days project, making it a fitting choice. However, the most exciting part is that Mackenyu, Netflix’s One Piece Zoro star, has been revealed as the actor playing the lead role of Mash Burnedead.

New information highlights that the role was offered to Mackenyu three years ago and that he has been building muscle for this particular character , rather than for Zoro. However, it was a blessing in disguise that Mackenyu ended up looking even more like Zoro in the second season. With these recent developments, Mashle is undoubtedly set to bloom with two major projects in the first half of 2027. Both projects are bound to give the manga series a boost as well, bringing much more attention to Shonen Jump’s underrated magical comedy, which blends the vibes of One-Punch Man and Harry Potter and deserves far more recognition.

title: 3 Zoro Moments That Prove He’s One Piece’s Perfect First Mate
content:
Any pirate across the course of history would be hard-pressed to find a better first mate than Roronoa Zoro in One Piece . The former bounty-hunting swordsman turned Straw-Hat Pirate, gives his all to his captain in every conflict and that’s what makes him the most loyal first mate in piracy. The second Zoro decided to join Monkey D. Luffy’s crew, he even gave up his greatest goal in favor of serving his captain’s every wish.

Luffy helped Zoro escape Marine captivity, and in return, Zoro said he’d become a criminal. He then added that his goal was to become “the world’s greatest swordsman ,” and he’d hold Luffy personally responsible for making him give up his dream if that happens along the way. Instead, the captain encouraged his dream all the more, saying that he’d expect nothing less as someone in service to the future King of the Pirates. Throughout the years, Luffy has held true to giving Zoro every shot at achieving his goal, and his first mate has repaid him with unmatched allegiance and selfless servitude.

3) Tries To Cut Off His Legs To Save Crew

An absolutely absurd situation occurs before One Piece even reaches the triple digits in episode count. Zoro, Nami and Vivi are slowly succumbing to No. 3’s horrifying wax-to-death attack, but the first mate refuses to go down without a fight, even if he can’t stand on his own two legs. Ever the crazy swordsman, he actually tries to sever his legs. Thankfully, Luffy returns in time to get them out of the mess, or Zoro might’ve accomplished it. He even jokes with Nami that he got halfway through.

An insane attempt on multiple levels. First, he’d just been dominated by the current world’s greatest swordsman in Dracule Mihawk a couple sagas ago. This move would’ve forever hampered his abilities to reach that goal and topple Mihawk, but Zoro’s dogged determination wouldn’t let his friends die for nothing. Second, even if he had gotten out of the trap, what would he have done with no legs? In an alternate universe, could he really take out the Baroque Works agents with no legs? Zoro likely believed he could or die trying. Either way, it made for an awesome scene, and one of his most selfless moments.

2) Impassioned Speech Backing Luffy’s Captainship

Zoro takes his duty as first mate seriously and there was no better example of that than when he stood up for Luffy when his role as captain came into question. Usopp challenges Luffy to a fight for ownership of the Going Merry. Unsurprisingly, Luffy wins the fight, and Usopp leaves the crew. No one threatens to leave after Usopp’s departure, but his first mate issues a two-fold speech backing the captain and essentially demanding more from him.

He states that Luffy is the captain regardless of his Laissez-Faire attitude and stupidity. Still, Zoro demands that he hold the crew to a standard and that means not letting Usopp back into the Straw Hats without an apology. It’s a time where the Straw Hats were splintering and instead of trying to take over the crew or endorse someone else, he proves once again that he’s the voice of reason. He gives a major vote of confidence to his captain.

1) Zoro Risks Life & Takes All Of Luffy’s Damage

This choice should come as no surprise, but this scene doesn’t get the credit it deserves. Luffy is on death’s door, and is about to be taken by Bartholomew Kuma, until Zoro comes to his rescue. With the captain incapacitated, Zoro strikes a deal with Kuma to trade his life for Luffy’s. Kuma agrees, as he can draw Luffy’s pain and fatigue out of his body and pass it to Zoro through what appears to be a bubble. However, Kuma advises the swordsman that the experience is likely to kill him.

He sends a small amount of the pain to Zoro, who convulses back and forth in extreme agony. Undeterred by the hellish experience, Zoro steps forward and presses both hands into the bubble which turns into a freeze frame scene. No one knows exactly what has become of Zoro when they wake up. Sanji is the first to find Zoro covered in blood, and asks Zoro what happened. To which Zoro simply answered that nothing happened.

This sacrifice is above and beyond the call of duty for any first mate. At this point, most people would’ve let Luffy get taken, especially after the initial taste of what the pain could do. This is the ultimate scene in what makes Zoro the perfect first mate. He’d literally risk his own life to save his captain and his captain’s dream. It’s one of the most selfless and humble act of the whole series and that’s saying a lot for a series that’s closing in on 1,200 episodes, and yet, it’s pure Zoro. What do you think? Are these the three most humble moments of Roronoa Zoro? Let us know in the comments.

title: Odd Taxi Manga Author Launches New Rematch With You Manga in Late November
content:
Manga creator Takeichi Abaraya announced on Wednesday that they will launch a new manga titled Rematch With You in Akita Shoten 's YanChan Web manga website later this month. Abaraya previously published a dōjin version of the manga titled "My last Match With You" at the Comitia event in November 2025. The manga also has its own official X/Twitter account .

Abaraya launched the manga adaptation of the Odd Taxi original anime in the Darupana website spinoff of Shogakukan 's Big Comic Superior magazine in January 2021, and ended it in June 2022. Shogakukan published five compiled book volumes for the manga. Denpa and KUMA licensed the manga, and will begin releasing the manga with the first volume in May 2027.

Abaraya launched the RoOT/Route of Odd Taxi (stylized with a backwards R in "RoOT") manga spinoff for Odd Taxi in Darupana in February 2023, and ended it in April 2025. Shogakukan published six volumes for the manga. The manga inspired a live-action television series that aired in April 2024. Crunchyroll streamed the series.

title: 3 Things You Need to Know Before Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2
content:
It’s only been around a week since Avatar: Seven Havens wrapped up its first season, leaving several questions unanswered. The franchise returned after 12 years with a new animation series for the first time in 12 years, and the wait was worth it as the latest installment earns praise for its exceptional worldbuilding and captivating characters. More than a year after it was officially announced, the series debuted in October this year and ended in the same month after releasing Episode 13. The series follows twin Earthbender sisters, Pavi and Nisha, as they navigate a world where the Avatar is feared among the masses rather than being treated as a savior.

The finale of Book 1 features Pavi heading off to the next Haven in order to help it and also figure out how to unlock the next of her seven chakras. This helps the franchise set up the overarching journey for the upcoming season, which means fans are in for a new adventure and exciting plot twists. There’s still a lot of things the story needs to resolve in the second season, but so far, there hasn’t been much information on the series’ future. Here’s everything you need to keep in mind while you wait for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2.

3) Avatar: Seven Havens Has Been Confirmed for Four Seasons

While the story is still in its initial phase, the animation series will release three more seasons over the next few years. Naturally, information regarding the plotlines and everything else will take some time, but this confirmation does establish the fact that the series has a bright future ahead of it. The first season was a huge success, and we can expect the same from the upcoming sequel seasons as well, depending on how the story is handled. Each season is expected to release 13 episodes and follow the same schedule. The show’s co-creator, Michael Dante DiMartino, confirmed this information in an interview after the first season’s finale while also sharing other plans regarding the series’ future. DiMartino also confirmed during the same interview that it will take a while for all four seasons to be released. However, since the sequels are still in their initial phase, there wasn’t much information for the co-creator to share.

2) Season 2 Has Yet to Confirm Any Release Window

While fans have been eagerly awaiting updates on the second season, it’s also important to note that the first season only wrapped up a week ago . This means that fans will have to wait at least a few weeks or even months to get any update on the second season. Since 2026 is almost over, we might have to wait until next year to know the release window of the second season. The show’s co-creator and the showrunners have also not revealed anything regarding when we can expect the animation series to return. However, at the very least, we know that it will return to Paramount+ since it’s the official streaming service for the series. Additionally, the animation series released batches of three to four episodes every Friday starting from October 9th to October 31st. We can expect the upcoming seasons to follow the same release format as well.

1) Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Won’t Have Major Time Skips

During the same interview with IGN where DiMartino confirmed the series will have four seasons, showrunner Sehaj Sethi also reveals major information regarding the second season’s plot. She reveals that the series doesn’t have any plans for a multi-year time jump, at least not yet. This means that the second season will pick up the story only a few weeks after the first season’s finale. The upcoming season needs to shed light on the twins’ journey and their struggles as they go their separate ways. While Pavi embarks on a journey across the Havens, Nisha decides to stay behind in Allora with Karthik. Unlike Pavi, she plans to help people while staying in the city. The twins won’t have been separate for long when the animation series returns, which is another reason to hope that they might be reunited sooner than we think.

What are you most excited to see in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2? What do you hope will happen next in the lives of Pavi and Nisha? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

What are you most excited to see in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2? What do you hope will happen next in the lives of Pavi and Nisha? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Paradox Live The Animation's Film Announces Title, 2027 Opening
content:
The official website for the hip-hop-themed multimedia franchise presented the early teaser visual for its upcoming film project on Friday. The visual announced the project's Paradox Live the Movie title and 2027 opening.

Studio GRAPH77 ( Tatsuki Fujimoto 17-26 's "Shikaku") is producing the film project. Nine teams with 29 characters will appear, including the characters who appeared in the previous television series as well as new characters.

Avex and GCREST 's hip-hop-themed multimedia franchise launched in November 2019. The story is set in the near future, when rappers wear accessories that contain a metallic substance called Phantom Metal. Through the Phantom Metal's chemical reaction with the rappers' own DNA, the rapper can create illusions linked to their emotions during their performance. The result is a new type of spectacular concert.

The television anime premiered on the Tokyo MX channel on October 3, 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan.

The franchise also includes CDs, merchandise, and concert events. The overall franchise 's "4th Season" story arc launched this past September.

title: Rainy Day Serenade Anime Reveals Key Visual, Teaser Trailer, Main Cast, April 2027 Premiere
content:
Rainy Day Serenade anime revealed a key visual and teaser trailer on Friday, featuring the main cast. An April 2027 release date and the main staff were also announced.

Yume Miyamoto stars in the series as Hina Katagiri alongside Takeo Otsuka who voices Takaaki Hongo. Tezuka Production is animating the series with Takashi Kamei as director. Yoko Yonaiyama is handling the series composition and Nobuteru Yuki is in charge of character designs.

The anime is based on a manga series written and illustrated by Haruka Kawachi, which was serialized in Kodansha’s josei manga magazine Kiss from November 2014 to November 2025. It has a total of 14 volumes. Kodansha USA is licensing the series in English as a 2-in-1 omnibus, with the first omnibus set to be released in January 2027. They describe it as: On rainy days, Hina has dreams about her younger self playing with a mysterious boy in a garden she’s never seen before—until, by chance, she stumbles upon the place. There’s a young man there, Takaaki, who mistakes Hina for his fiancée Hinako. He whisks her back to what he thinks is her home, where Hina’s doppelganger is waiting, and Hina realizes this isn’t the Tokyo she left behind but Japan in the year 1907! Is this all a dream or something much stranger? Source: Rainy Day Serenade anime official website , X (formerly Twitter) ©Haruka Kawachi/Kodansha/”Rainy Day Serenade” Production Committee

title: 'Namidaame to Serenade' Reveals Main Cast, Staff, Teaser Promo, Spring 2027 Premiere
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Haruka Kawachi 's Namidaame to Serenade ( Rainy Day Serenade ) manga revealed the main cast, staff, the first key visual (pictured right), a celebratory illustration drawn by the creator (pictured center), and a teaser promotional video on Friday. The anime is scheduled to premiere in April 2027.

Voice actors Yume Miyamoto ( Yomi no Tsugai ) and Takeo Ootsuka ( Medalist ) are starring in the anime as Hina Katagiri and Takaaki Hongou, respectively.

Staff Director: Takashi Kamei ( My Home Hero ) Series Composition: Youko Yonaiyama ( Kamiina Botan, Yoeru Sugata wa Yuri no Hana ) Character Design: Nobuteru Yuuki ( Under Ninja ) Art Director: Hiroshi Katou ( Mao ) Color Design: Kunio Tsujita ( Tokyo Revengers: Seiya Kessen-hen ) Director of Photography: Yoshie Itou ( Boku no Tsuma wa Kanjou ga Nai ) Studio: Tezuka Productions

Kawachi serialized the josei romance manga in Kiss from November 2014 to November 2025. Kodansha published the 14th and final volume on February 13.

Kodansha USA licensed the manga in English on January 9, and the first volume is scheduled to be released on January 19, 2027.

title: Manga 'Killing Bites' Concludes with 28th Volume
content:
Shinya Murata and Kazasa Sumita 's Killing Bites manga ended its serialization on October 23. The 145th and final chapter marked the end of its nearly 13-year run. The 28th and final volume is scheduled to be released on December 25.

In the commemorative message , Murata expressed his gratitude to readers who had followed the manga throughout its nearly 13-year serialization. He also reflected on the central question behind the story, "What is the strongest beast?" Describing it as a question whose answer belongs to the readers and is reflected in the manga's conclusion. Murata encouraged readers to continue contemplating the question and find their own answers.

Sumita also shared a commemorative message, reflecting on the manga's journey, recalling how the story began with Hitomi and gradually introduced numerous animal characters. He also noted that he had initially envisioned Nomoto, an ordinary college student, as a character whose personal growth would signify the story's success. Sumita expressed his gratitude to the readers, assistants, and editorial staff for their support throughout the manga's 13-year serialization.

Murata began writing the action ecchi manga illustrated by Sumita in Monthly Hero's magazine in November 2013. Following the magazine's discontinuation in October 2020, the series moved to the Comiplex website in November of that year. Hero published the 27th volume on June 29. The manga has a cumulative 500,000 copies of its volumes in circulation in October 2017.

A spin-off manga, titled Hoshigari Sugi desho!? Inaba-san , was serialized on the Wild Hero's from August 2020 to November 2022. The third and final volume went on sale in December 2022.

MediBang Global licensed the manga in English in January 2023. Comikey also released the manga in March 2023.

A 12-episode television anime adaptation produced by LIDENFILMS aired in Winter 2018. Sentai Filmworks licensed the anime in North America and released it on home video in October 2020.

Special manga site: http://www.heros-web.com/works/killing.html Special manga X: @ killingbites
